Hsiu, Andrew. 2016. The classification of Cosao: a Lolo-Burmese language of China and Laos. Handout (11 pp.) and slides, 22nd Himalayan Languages Symposium, IIT Guwahati, 8-10 June 2016. Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.1127810.
sources.note: Nothing. Comparative-lexical classification paper; Cosao forms are cited with Chao tone numbers (e.g. tsʰo55 sɔ55, u31 kʰja31, mja33 sɯ53), notes two sound correspondences with Khir (Cl- : Cj-, -ŋ : -m); no word on stress or accent.

sources.citation: Bai, Bibo & Xu, Xianming. 2015. Documentation of endangered Cosao "green codes" in Yunnan, China. Slides presented at the 4th International Conference on Language Documentation and Conservation (ICLDC), Honolulu, 27 Feb 2015.http://hdl.handle.net/10125/25306
sources.note: Nothing. Ethnobotanical 'plant code' talk; states only that Cosao is a Southern Yi (Loloish) Tibeto-Burman language without writing; a few plant names given with tone numbers (sɯ31 ho).

sources.note: The only first-hand description of Cosao (Glottolog listed by Glottolog as a grammar; Grambank's sole source). Chapter 2 语音 will give 声母/韵母/声调 and, if anything is said about stress or weak (轻声) syllables, it will be there. Not in HathiTrust, archive.org, or any open repository; print only (Douban/JD list copies for sale).
